brief.headline: Memory supercycle intact: DRAM +58-63% QoQ Q2, NAND +70-75% QoQ; HBM capacity crunch persists; leverage restrictions cap Samsung/SKH rally
brief.summary: <cite index="14-2,14-7">DRAM contract prices to rise 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, NAND Flash 70-75% QoQ per TrendForce</cite>, following <cite index="14-8">Q1 gains of 90-95% for DRAM and ~60% for NAND</cite>. <cite index="22-2,22-6">US hyperscalers committed $660-690B capex in 2026, nearly doubling 2025 levels, with vast majority directed at AI compute and data centers</cite>. <cite index="6-1">Goldman Sachs forecasts 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026</cite> as <cite index="12-9,12-10">SK Hynix signals DRAM supply remains constrained through 2H26, NAND at similar levels</cite>. <cite index="31-7">NVIDIA secured over 60% of TSMC CoWoS capacity for 2025-2026</cite>, but <cite index="32-1,32-2">tight CoWoS supply pushing SK Hynix to work with Intel on advanced packaging</cite>. <cite index="39-5,39-6">Wall Street banks restricting hedge fund leverage on Samsung, SK Hynix, and TSM; Samsung intraday gain retreated from 12% to under 8%, SK Hynix from 9% to under 4% on June 12</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="38-5,38-6,38-9">Combined Q2 operating profit projected to exceed 150T won: Samsung 88.3T won, SK Hynix 64.3T won</cite>. SK Hynix maintains pure-play HBM leverage with <cite index="5-5">industry positioning as primary anchor delivering both HBM3E and HBM4 reliably</cite>, while <cite index="40-6">Samsung in close discussion to supply HBM4 to Nvidia</cite>. <cite index="44-1,44-2">SK Hynix tripled YTD, Samsung up 175%; together 53% of KOSPI, more than double their weight five years ago</cite>. Near-term catalyst symmetry on <cite index="3-3">Samsung expanding HBM capacity ~50% in 2026, SK Hynix increasing infrastructure investment more than 4x prior guidance</cite>. Long Samsung vs. SK Hynix not compelling—both benefit from same structural tailwinds, but leverage restrictions and position limits pose symmetric technical risk. Pair neutral; beta preference shifts to SK Hynix if CoWoS diversification accelerates via Intel partnership.

memory_cycle.stage: Mid-supercycle: pricing acceleration intact, supply deficit through 2H26
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="5-11">BofA defines 2026 as supercycle similar to 1990s boom, forecasting DRAM revenue +51% YoY, NAND +45% YoY, with ASPs rising 33% and 26% respectively</cite>. <cite index="10-3,10-4">Widening supply-demand gap driven by CSPs securing capacity and suppliers maintaining disciplined output; manufacturers reallocating advanced nodes toward server DRAM and HBM for AI demand</cite>. <cite index="12-6,12-7">Production cuts in 2024-2025 tightened availability across commodity DRAM and NAND, particularly DDR4 and legacy nodes for industrial/automotive</cite>. <cite index="14-10,14-12">CSPs securing bulk of supply via long-term agreements; meaningful capacity expansion not expected until late 2027</cite>. Cycle durability supported by <cite index="5-8,5-9">structural increase in DRAM and HBM installed per AI server, plus rising enterprise SSD demand</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="8-3,8-4,8-5">Nvidia testing 16-layer HBM for delivery as early as Q4 2026, forcing Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron into race to meet next-gen AI accelerator requirements; discussions exploratory, no contracts signed but triggered internal planning on yields and volumes</cite>. <cite index="2-4,2-5,2-6">Korean memory manufacturer researcher cites industry discussions on separating GPUs and HBM into separate packages connected via optical links, potentially allowing several times more HBM than existing designs</cite>. <cite index="40-1,40-5">Samsung and SK Hynix struck letter of intent with OpenAI for 900,000 DRAM wafers/month to meet Stargate project memory demands</cite>. <cite index="7-14">Global memory shortage enabling Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung to hike prices</cite>. HBM remains the clearest margin accretion vector for both names through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Wall Street banks restrict leverage on Samsung, SK Hynix, TSM; stocks retreat mid-session June 12
news_pulse.implication: Technical headwind: forced deleveraging could pressure near-term price action despite fundamental strength; passive selling estimated at $69B since Oct 2025 per Goldman due to concentration limits

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix Q2 operating profit projected to exceed 150T won combined on memory boom
news_pulse.implication: Record earnings confirm pricing power intact; Samsung DS division accounting for ~95% of total operating profit signals foundry/LSI drag persists

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS shortage drives SK Hynix-Intel 2.5D packaging collaboration
news_pulse.implication: Supply chain diversification positive for SK Hynix; reduces single-point packaging dependency and accelerates HBM+logic integration timelines if Intel 2.5D yields ramp

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia exploring 16-layer HBM delivery by Q4 2026, pressures memory makers on development schedules
news_pulse.implication: Technology roadmap acceleration increases capex/yield risk but extends HBM ASP premium runway; SK Hynix best positioned on 12-layer HBM4 ramp

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices to rise 58-63% QoQ Q2 2026, NAND +70-75% per TrendForce
news_pulse.implication: Pricing momentum exceeds Q1 gains (DRAM +90-95%, NAND ~60%); NAND now outpacing DRAM QoQ for first time in cycle, driven by enterprise SSD pull-in

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex consensus at $725B, up from $670B pre-earnings; Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet driving incremental spend
news_pulse.implication: Demand signal upgrade supports memory supply deficit thesis; Meta cited higher component pricing as driver for $10B capex raise at both ends of guidance

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix expand capacity: Samsung targeting ~50% HBM increase in 2026, SK Hynix investing 4x prior infrastructure guidance
news_pulse.implication: Capex ramp confirms multi-year supply constraint; Samsung P5 fab operational by 2028, SK Hynix M15X by mid-2027 means 2026-2027 pricing protected

news_pulse.headline: Goldman Sachs forecasts 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026; supercycle extends past 2028
news_pulse.implication: Validates structural undersupply; low inventory levels amplify pricing volatility risk but support ASP sustainability through 2027

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI 200 futures volatility elevated post-June 12 leverage news; options skew likely tilted put-heavy near-term as hedge funds adjust gross exposure. Samsung/SK Hynix ADR premiums compressed. Monitor 1-month ATM vol and basis vs. KRW-hedged levels for re-entry signal once deleveraging flow exhausts. Long-dated calls (6M+) offer asymmetry if hyperscaler capex revisions continue.
